access: Cannot currently be played: The Judge has been closed for renovation since 1 December 2025, and the operator projects reopening in October 2026 ("a planned reopening in Fall 2026") with no specific day published and the schedule stated as weather-dependent. When open it is daily-fee public. Capitol Hill's other public course, The Legislator, carries no 2026 closure; the Senator hosts the LPGA Epson Tour Guardian Championship 11-13 September 2026, and public access that week is unpublished.
facility: Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail at Capitol Hill

access: A Municipality of Anchorage public facility, open to anyone with no membership or residency requirement. The standard advance booking window is five days, with an explicit out-of-state exception letting travellers request tee times earlier through the course's Out of State page.

No membership required. Book online through EzLinks (quintero2.ezlinksgolf.com, or quinteroazres1.ezlinksgolf.com for single players) up to 90 days ahead; a credit card is required and cancellation is 48 hours. Golf Digest labels the course "Public" while operator Troon's own page says "Semi-private"; the guide publishes the disagreement unresolved.

Open to the public. The operator's own words: "Operating as a semi-private club, Mystic Creek has membership opportunities available and is also open to the public." The Public Tee Times link routes to a login-free booking page, and membership affects only a Troon discount tier - there is no booking-window, sponsor or residency rule. Closed every Monday, and closed 14-20 September 2026 for the El Dorado Shootout.

Open to the public, but the tee sheet is gated by a hotel stay. Guests of Pebble Beach Resorts — The Lodge at Pebble Beach, The Inn at Spanish Bay, Casa Palmero — reserve up to 18 months ahead, subject to a minimum stay the resort does not publish as a fixed figure; non-guests can reserve only 24 hours ahead. A cart fee is mandatory for non-resort guests.

Members-first club. Non-members book by phone at (970) 663-5063 up to seven days ahead, Monday to Thursday after 11am and Friday to Sunday after 1pm; Thursday through Sunday is reserved to the membership and the TPC Network, with leftover times released 24 hours out. The operator's own overlapping wording leaves Thursday contested, and the guide leaves it contested.

A "public, daily-fee operation" in the operator's own Terms, with its FAQ answering "No" on memberships and non-affiliates booking ten days ahead. No affiliation is required: the operator prices a Yale Affiliate Guest rate as a separate row from the $350 Non-Affiliate rate, so a traveller simply pays the higher row. Rank 1 fails on both its label and its member-login terms. Note the ranking's own label moved: this course reads Private in the August 2025, October 2025 and February 2026 captures and Public live, under an identical edition string, so the row rests on the operator's terms rather than on the rubric.
second_course: The Tradition Golf Club at Oak Lane

access: The ranking's only Public entry of five, re-established from scratch by three methods with exactly five rubric elements for five entries, so no label is missing. The operator publishes no green fee that carries a date -- its rate page reads "Dynamic Pricing", its booking engine returned Cloudflare challenges to four separate clients, and its third-party tee-time channel was empty on five sampled dates -- so no fee is publishable for the state.

Publicly playable, established by executing the operator's own tee-sheet service unauthenticated: 47 rows returned for the Stadium Course on 12 September 2026, two of them fully open, and 73 rows for Dye's Valley with 46 fully open. The same service corroborates a published closure, returning all 79 of 79 Dye's Valley rows blocked on 8 September 2026. The operator's rate table carries no year and no effective date, so no green fee is publishable; the only dated prices it publishes are stay-and-play packages.
course: THE PLAYERS Stadium Course at TPC Sawgrass
second_course: Dye's Valley Course at TPC Sawgrass

access: The longest walk in the corpus: thirty-six higher entries fail either the ranking's own label or the operator's terms. The ranking's rubric field is not stable -- #23 McLemore carried "Public" through the 8 March 2026 capture and fails the operator test, and #32 Currahee carries "Public" while its own site reads "Private Golf & Lake Community", the archived 2023-'26 edition having labelled it Private at #21 -- so every rejection above rank 37 rests on the operator's own terms rather than on the label. The operator publishes no dated rate qualifier, so no green fee is publishable.

Golf Digest labels the course "Public," but a non-resort guest cannot play it at all: Four Seasons Resort Lanai states on two of its own pages, "Course access is not available for day guest use," and no green fee, tee-time page or non-guest rate for a day visitor exists anywhere on the operator's site. Play is confined to resort guests. Hours are Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays.

Public access through the club's own site or by phone at 1-800-523-2464, with no membership and no hotel stay required. In peak season, 18 May to 13 September, phone bookings are capped at 45 days ahead while online booking runs beyond it; Coeur d'Alene Tribal Members are exempt. Resort lodging confers no tee-time priority — the Stay & Play package affects price only.

Daily-fee public, with no membership and no resident or non-resident tiering. Online tee times run up to 60 days ahead through ForeUp, or by phone at 866-264-4455, with the card charged at booking. Aerification closes the course 14-17 April and, tentatively, 20-23 October.
course: Cog Hill Golf & Country Club: Course No. 4 – Dubsdread

access: Playable with no overnight stay required. The resort's FAQ names both ranked courses and answers "Is an overnight reservation required to book a tee time?" with "No." Non-guests book by telephone within a fourteen-day window; the resort's online booking system exposes one bookable course and carries no Pete Dye tee sheet at all. The published rate figures carry no dated qualifier.
course: The Pete Dye Course at French Lick Resort
second_course: The Donald Ross Course at French Lick Resort

access: Daily-fee public course with no membership. The operator's own policy page states "Starting times may be reserved up to 14 days in advance"; groups of sixteen or more book through the pro shop, and cancellation notice is 24 hours.

Public and Kansas State University-owned, with no membership or residency requirement. Booking runs from colberthills.com out to colberthills.cps.golf, whose reservation subdomain 403s and has never been archived, so the days-in-advance window is unsourceable and is stated as such rather than invented. The 2026 seasonal rates of $115/$105/$80 (1 April to 10 November, cart included) carry the operator's own "rates change through the season" qualifier. The whole facility closes 13-15 and 27-29 September, 26 November and 24-25 December 2026.
Public, with no membership required. Tee times book online through Chronogolf on a seven-day public booking window, with 24-hour cancellation and payment at the course (3% card fee). Closed Mondays.
course: Park Mammoth Golf Club: Park Mammoth
second_course: Barren River Lake State Park Golf Course

access: Public, and no annual pass is required - the finder's "annual passes only" reading was dissolved by executing the operator's own ezLinks booking API after its engine-blocked claim failed. A visitor books a single round at the Non-Resident tier, $119-$299 for 18 holes, on a 136-day public booking window with 48-hour cancellation.

An access shape the corpus meets only here: in the operator's own words a "private club, which welcomes public play", with public players calling the Golf Shop three days in advance. No sponsorship, referral, reciprocal-club or host requirement exists anywhere on the site -- the three-day phone window is the whole constraint. Rank 1 fails on its own terms, not merely on its label: "exclusive private club... members-only setting", cottages and villas only, with no non-guest rate. Neither course dates its rate table, so no green fee is publishable, and the operator publishes no opening or closing date -- an absence confirmed across 13 live pages and 14 archived captures including deep winter.

Daily-fee and publicly playable, the first Public-labelled entry on the ranking: ranks 1 through 8 were each verified Private inside their own blocks by two independent methods, and Golf Digest's own course page records the facility type as Public. The operator publishes a dated "2026 Rate Schedule". Note that the ranking's Public label is not reliable on its own here -- rank 14 carries it while being a Troon Prive member club -- so each rejection above rank 9 was checked against the operator's own terms.

The operator's own words: "The golf course and the restaurant are open to the public", with no affiliation qualifier found across eleven pages despite the club's college association. Ranks 1 to 12 carry a Private rubric inside their own DOM blocks across three genuinely distinct captures, and eight are additionally confirmed private on their operators' own terms. An unaccompanied-guest rate is published but carries no dated qualifier -- the page footer's year moved from 2025 to 2026 while the table did not -- so no green fee is publishable. The operator does publish a dated season: the course opens 15 April 2026 and closes 15 November 2026.

Daily-fee with no membership - Golf Digest records the facility type as Daily Fee and the course as not private. Reservations are required, though walk-ons are taken when possible; players register in the golf shop, and booking is limited to the current calendar year. Cancellation is a 7-day window charging 100% per player and may vary by group size - the FAQ's four-tier and the rates page's three-tier schedules differ, and both are stated. The 2026 season runs 1 April to 30 November.
course: Arcadia Bluffs Golf Club: The Bluffs Course
second_course: Arcadia Bluffs Golf Club: The South Course

access: Public course, no membership required. Booking is phone-only at (218) 865-8030 - every "Book Tee Times" control on the resort's site is a tel: link and there is no online tee sheet. The 2026 rate table runs $100/$130/$130/$100 across four seasonal bands with a $75 replay, and the 48-hour notice governs cancellation, not booking. Late Season runs 28 September to 11 October 2026; the 2026 opening date is published only as "TBD."

Open to the general public with no stay, host or credit-line requirement; the operator's own page states the course is "Available to resort guests, club members, and the general public," and the only "required" anywhere on the site is the dress code. The Azaleas is usually closed Monday and The Oaks usually closed Tuesday.
second_course: Dancing Rabbit Golf Club: The Oaks

access: Public resort course, no membership. Non-resort guests book up to 30 days ahead - 60 days for play falling 15 June to 15 August - at book.rguest.com or 1-800-225-6343; resort guests book by phone only, at the resort rate. The course closes for aeration 8-10 September 2026, with recovery to 20 September, and off-season 1 January to 5 March and 7 to 31 December.

Open to non-member and non-resort-guest play after 12:00 PM in the 2026 season; no membership and no resort room required. Book at wildernessclub.ezlinksgolf.com or call (406) 296-8264. Operator Escalante Golf stated a 2024 intent to eventually go fully private; that is an intent, not the current rule. No dated green fee is published.

Public daily-fee course with no membership tier - the operator states "We do not currently offer memberships." Tee times are booked online through ForeUp for 2026 and Whoosh from 2027, on a $25 per-golfer nonrefundable deposit; cancelling outside a week refunds everything but the deposit, inside a week nothing. $160 per golfer with cart. The 2026 season runs 16 May to 1 October.

Golf Digest labels it "Public," but the operator's own terms are narrower: a qualifying MGM Resorts hotel stay is required to be considered. On weekdays a hotel guest requests a time through the concierge; weekends are held for comped players with a casino host and a gambling credit line. There is no public tee sheet.

The championship fallback applies, on the best-proved negative in this corpus: the state's 2025-'26 ranking has exactly five entries, five rubric elements against five titles, all Private, with "Public" occurring zero times -- reproduced on a live fetch and six distinct captures reaching back to March 2025, and all five operators confirming their own gates verbatim. The course is public daily-fee, on a record of 19 New Hampshire Opens, more than any course in that championship's history, re-derived from the association's venue-by-year table. Its rate card carries a dated qualifier -- "Rates listed here are current as of January 1, 2026" -- so the fee is publishable. The state's best-known golf resort is genuinely public in its own words but loses on record, four hostings to nineteen.

The championship fallback applies: no entry on the state's 2025-'26 ranking is publicly accessible at any rank. All 25 entries carry a Private rubric -- 25 rubric elements against 25 title elements, so no entry is unlabelled -- established across two archived captures from different source WARCs and a live fetch. The one entry labelled Public in an earlier capture of the same edition is refused in writing by its operator's management group: "Membership is closed. Future consideration is by referral only." The Bay Course is daily-fee resort golf, host of the ShopRite LPGA and part of the 1942 PGA Championship. No green fee carries a dated qualifier, so none is publishable.
Public daily-fee, with no membership required. Online booking runs 30 days ahead; beyond that window a tee time is requested by phone.

Publicly playable by a non-resident, proved by executing the state's own booking system: the "Non Resident" class is the only unprotected one on the Black tee sheet, and a credential-free query returned a real bookable 18-hole time at $88, while the "Resident" class returned HTTP 401. Residency is a preference rather than a requirement -- a seven-day booking window instead of five, and roughly double the rate -- and there is no lottery. The operator states it plainly: "There is no residency requirement on the Blue, Green and Yellow Courses." The engine's figures match the operator's own rate sheet dated 4/22/2026, so the fee is publishable.

Daily-fee and publicly playable: the course's own booking API, called unauthenticated, returns bookable slots under a rate plan the operator itself names "Public 18 Holes". The eleven higher-ranked entries do not qualify. Ranks 2, 8 and 9 are Pinehurst courses labelled "Public" by the ranking and excluded by Pinehurst's own terms, which read: "To play Courses No. 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, or 11, you must be a member or resort guest." Tobacco Road publishes no dated rate qualifier — its page states that displayed rates are real-time pricing — so no green fee is publishable for it.
second_course: The Golf Club at Quail Ridge

access: No published non-member booking route. Golf Digest ranks it first and labels it "Public," with a "Daily Fee" facility type and a $105 weekend fee as of the ranking data's own 14 November 2025 update; the club's own site calls itself "a private club," puts every booking control behind a member login, and publishes no green fee and no guest policy. The only sourced avenue is the phone, (701) 852-3591. The guide publishes the disagreement between the two sources rather than resolving it.

Daily-fee and publicly playable, proved by executing the operator's own Club Caddie booking engine: 21, 37 and 54 bookable slots across three sampled dates, with every pricing plan carrying the operator's own "Public" title type and no guest rate. The walk is the joint-longest in the corpus outside Georgia -- ranks 1 through 15 each carry an explicit Private rubric bound inside their own block, confirmed in two independent archived captures and a live fetch, with no entry on the page lacking a rubric.

Genuinely public, no membership. The club's own site injects a JavaScript-only Chronogolf widget resolving to chronogolf.com/club/jimmie-austin-golf-course, with no login; the public player type books up to seven days ahead, confirmed both by the widget's own configuration and by the booking API's refusal text. On 6 September 2026 it quoted $105.75 weekday and $133.33 weekend for 18 holes, plus $18.39 for a shared cart, paid at the course. A single player cannot complete a booking online alone.
course: Jimmie Austin Golf Club at the University of Oklahoma
facility: Jimmie Austin Golf Club at the University of Oklahoma

access: Public (Golf Digest label). Daily-fee resort course: the resort publishes a day-guest green fee for every month of the year. Day guests booking inside 21 days pay the standard day-guest rate; booking more than 21 days ahead requires an April-to-mid-November date, the premium day-guest rate, a tee time after 10:00 a.m., and no more than one year in advance. Resort lodging guests book earlier and at the lower resort-guest rate.

Access tiered by price rather than gated, and dated: the resort publishes a "Non-resort guest rates" column under a "2026 Old Course Fees" heading at $289, held constant on every Friday-to-Sunday slot sampled, with no stay required -- so the fee is publishable. Twenty-six higher entries fail on their rubric or on their operators' own words; two of them read "Open to overnight guests and all-access members", and their supposed public tee-time package was established not to exist in the booking provider's system. The second course was checked rather than assumed despite its fraternal name: its own booking engine serves anonymous callers the non-member rate channel.
course: The Old Course at Bedford Springs

access: Rank 7 is the first and only Public label on a seven-course list: ranks 1 through 6 are each labelled Private, so the selection is forced rather than chosen, the same single-Public shape as Iowa. The label is printed on Rhode Island's own per-state page, which is where §1's open condition 1 asked each wave to read it rather than trusting the every-state summary. Access rests on the operator as well as the label, after Connecticut's moved between captures: newportnational.com states "The Golf Course is Open to the Public!" in its own words. No green fee is publishable -- the operator's site carries no rates, no seasonal variation and no dated pricing at all, the same refusal Massachusetts made for a different reason. The opening year is absent from the operator's site and is not published.
course: Newport National Golf Club: Orchard Course

access: Playable without a resort booking, and access is tiered by price rather than gated. The resort's own booking system, called unauthenticated, returns bookable tee times under rate types the operator names "(Walk w/ Caddie) Non Resort" and "(Walk w/o Caddie) Non Resort". Those non-guest rates appear inside a 60-day window and are absent beyond it, a boundary reproduced by date sweep. The resort publishes no green-fee rate card.
course: Kiawah Island Golf Resort: The Ocean Course
second_course: Kiawah Island Golf Resort: Osprey Point

access: Public course, no membership required. Non-members book on the club's own tee sheet at redrock.cps.golf (Club Prophet Systems) or by phone at (605) 718-4710. How far ahead a time may be taken is published nowhere reachable - the booking engine 403s behind Cloudflare and no archived capture carries it - so the advance-booking window is stated as unknown rather than estimated.
course: The Golf Club At Red Rock
facility: The Golf Club At Red Rock

access: Selected by the set's fallback criterion rather than by ranking: all fifteen entries on Golf Digest's Tennessee list are labelled Private, so no course satisfied the ranking criterion, and General's Retreat was taken on its competitive record - it hosted the LPGA Sara Lee Classic from 1988 to 1999, a twelve-edition run belonging to this course rather than to the Hermitage complex. Genuinely public: the foreUP booking API returned 28 bookable tee times with no authentication and no booking class, quoting an $84 green fee plus $16 cart for Sunday 20 September 2026, matching the published Friday-to-Sunday rate to the cent.
county: Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County

access: Daily-fee public. The operator's own booking system opens to public golfers seven days ahead at $350 per player, observed September 2026; a caddie is mandatory year-round, $80-$125 plus tax or $40-$120 plus tax for a forecaddie, putting an all-in public round at roughly $475-$525 per player. Resort guests book 120 days ahead and Frisco residents 10.

Non-members book by phone at 435-222-7830 or online through Chronogolf, on a 30-day public booking window stated by the operator. A room booking is optional and affects price only ($250-450 seasonal tiers); solo online booking is restricted. The course is closed to all play September 14 to October 6, 2026 for the PGA TOUR event.

Open to the public in the operator's own words -- "Highland Course | Open to general public, members and resort guests" -- and proved by executing its tee-time API unauthenticated, which returned 33 bookable slots at $325 for 20-21 September 2026 with no restrictions attached, 93 at $275 in November, none in December, and 87 at $225 in April 2027. Ranks 1 to 3 are private and member-gated on their own sites. The resort publishes dated 2026 Peak and Non-Peak rate headings.

Public course, no membership required. Walking only, with a push/pull cart included; book online at chambersbaygolf.com or call 253-460-4653. Residency-based rates open up to three months ahead from the first of the month; the non-resident prepaid tier opens January 1 for April-to-October play. Single players may join an existing group but cannot book an open time. Cancellation terms are tiered.

Playable at a published non-guest price rather than by exclusion. The resort's rate page carries a "Non-Registered" column beside "Registered Guests", and its memberships sell a discount off green fees rather than the right to play. A tee-time request form present in the operator's own sitemap, though unlinked from the golf section, lists The Old White and requires an answer to "Do you have an accommodation booked?" that offers "No". No online tee sheet exists, so no booking was executed. The rate page carries no dated qualifier.

Public, with no resort stay required - Kohler's own FAQ confirms non-guests may play. The resort's reservations page splits booking by lead time: inside 30 days, book online; beyond 30 days, and for every package, call 855-444-2838 or use the golf inquiry form. The same FAQ flags a Straits-specific warning that non-resort guests "may have booking restrictions" which no page anywhere specifies; the guide publishes that caveat live and unresolved rather than folding it into the 30-day rule.

Semi-private, with no lodging or membership requirement. Non-members play a fixed 1pm-2pm afternoon block daily, but booking itself is unrestricted — online at any hour, or by phone; the block governs play, not booking. The 2026 daily fee is $195 through May 22 and $300 from May 23 to close, including tax, cart and practice. Open early May to mid-October.
